nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps and $t'$ is reducible, then $t$ is reducible.
nodes.title: Reducibility is closed under backward evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $u$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, and $t'$ and $u$ have the same result, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.
nodes.title: Left expansion preserves having the same result

nodes.summary: Let $t$, $u$ and $u'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $u$ reduces to $u'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, and $t$ and $u'$ have the same result, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.
nodes.title: Right expansion preserves having the same result

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps and $t'$ terminates, then $t$ terminates.
nodes.title: Termination is closed under backward evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a term of type $A \Rightarrow B$ and let $a$, $a'$ be terms of type $A$, all in the same context. If $f$ is a value and $a$ evaluates to $a'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then the application $f\,a$ evaluates to $f\,a'$ in zero or more steps.
nodes.title: Evaluating the argument of a value function is a multi-step congruence

nodes.summary: Let $f$ and $f'$ be terms of type $A \Rightarrow B$ and let $a$ be a term of type $A$, all in the same context. If $f$ evaluates to $f'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then the application $f\,a$ evaluates to $f'\,a$ in zero or more steps.
nodes.title: Multi-step evaluation is a congruence in function position

nodes.summary: Let $f$ and $g$ be closed terms of a function type $A \Rightarrow B$, and let $a$ and $b$ be closed terms of type $A$. If $f$ and $g$ have the same result and $a$ and $b$ have the same result, then the applications $f\,a$ and $g\,b$ have the same result.
nodes.title: Application preserves having the same result

nodes.summary: For every closed term $f$ of a function type $A \Rightarrow B$ there is a term $b$ of type $B$ in the context with a single variable of type $A$ such that $f$ reduces, in zero or more call-by-value steps, to the lambda abstraction with body $b$.
nodes.title: Closed functions evaluate to lambda abstractions

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution that sends each variable of a context $\Gamma$ to a closed term of the same type, and let $a$ be a closed term of type $A$. If $\sigma$ and $a$ are reducible, then so is the substitution on the context $A, \Gamma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable $x$ to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.title: Extending a reducible substitution by a reducible term keeps it reducible

nodes.summary: Every substitution from the empty context to closed terms is reducible, since the empty context has no variables.
nodes.title: Substitutions on the empty context are reducible

nodes.summary: Let $v$ and $t$ be terms of the same type in the same context. If $v$ is a value and $v$ reduces to $t$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $v = t$.
nodes.title: Values reduce only to themselves

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ is reducible and $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t'$ is reducible.
nodes.title: Reducibility is closed under forward evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ terminates and $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t'$ terminates.
nodes.title: Termination is closed under forward evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, and let $\sigma$ be a reducible substitution sending each variable of $\Gamma$ to a closed term of the same type. Then the closed term obtained by applying $\sigma$ to $t$ is reducible.
nodes.title: Fundamental theorem of the reducibility relation

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t$ is reducible if and only if $t'$ is reducible.
nodes.title: Reducibility is invariant under evaluation

nodes.summary: A closed well-typed term $t$ normalizes, that is, reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a normal form (a term with no further reduction step), if and only if it terminates, that is, reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a value.
nodes.title: Normalization and termination coincide

nodes.summary: In the pure, constant-free calculus there is no closed term whose type is a base type.
nodes.title: No closed terms of base type

nodes.summary: If a closed term $t$ reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a normal form $n$ and also to a normal form $m$, then $n = m$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of normal forms

nodes.summary: Every closed well-typed term normalizes: it reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a normal form.
nodes.title: Normalization of closed terms

nodes.summary: A closed term $t$ of the simply typed lambda calculus normalizes when it reduces, in zero or more call-by-value steps, to a term in normal form, that is, a term with no further call-by-value reduction step.
nodes.title: Normalizing closed terms

nodes.summary: If a closed term $t$ reduces to a term $u$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.
nodes.title: Evaluation preserves the result of a closed term

nodes.summary: Every closed term of the simply typed lambda calculus that is a value terminates.
nodes.title: Values terminate

nodes.summary: Every closed well-typed term of the simply typed lambda calculus is reducible.
nodes.title: Closed terms are reducible

nodes.summary: A substitution $\sigma$ that replaces each variable of a context $\Gamma$ by a closed term of the same type is reducible when $\sigma(x)$ is reducible for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Reducible substitutions

nodes.summary: Reducibility of a closed term $t$ is defined by recursion on its simple type. At a base type, $t$ is reducible when it terminates. At a function type $A \Rightarrow B$, $t$ is reducible when it terminates and, for every reducible closed term $a$ of type $A$, the application $t\,a$ is reducible.
nodes.title: Tait reducibility for closed terms

nodes.summary: Every closed term has the same result as itself.
nodes.title: Reflexivity of having the same result

nodes.summary: For every simple type $A$, the relation of having the same result is an equivalence relation on the closed terms of type $A$.
nodes.title: Having the same result is an equivalence relation

nodes.summary: Two closed terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type have the same result when there is a value $v$ such that both $t$ and $u$ reduce to $v$ in zero or more call-by-value steps.
nodes.title: Closed terms with the same result

nodes.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be terms of the same type in the same context, with $v$ a value. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ and $t$ evaluates to $t'$, each in finitely many call-by-value steps, then $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in finitely many steps.
nodes.title: Evaluation to a value passes through every reduct

nodes.summary: If closed terms $t$ and $u$ have the same result, then $u$ and $t$ have the same result.
nodes.title: Symmetry of having the same result

nodes.summary: Every reducible closed term of the simply typed lambda calculus terminates.
nodes.title: Reducible terms terminate

nodes.summary: Every closed well-typed term evaluates, in finitely many call-by-value steps, to a value.
nodes.title: Termination of the call-by-value simply typed lambda calculus

nodes.summary: A closed term $t$ terminates when it evaluates, in finitely many call-by-value steps, to a value.
nodes.title: Termination of closed terms

nodes.summary: If closed terms $t$ and $u$ have the same result, and $u$ and a closed term $v$ have the same result, then $t$ and $v$ have the same result.
nodes.title: Transitivity of having the same result

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a term in any context. If $t$ reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a value $v$ and also to a value $w$, then $v = w$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the value reached by evaluation

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
